deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is page 2 of a printed German textbook in Fraktur type, interleaved or annotated in Gauss's copy. The bundle name 'HB.Leiste' points to Christian Leiste's school textbook 'Die Arithmetik und Algebra zum Gebrauch bey dem Unterricht' (Wolfenbüttel, c. 1790); this identification is my inference.

The printed text continues the introductory §1, a classification of applied mathematics:
(1b) Light refracted in transparent bodies of different density, especially ground glasses, belongs to Dioptrik.
(1c) The appearances of the heavenly bodies, their mutual positions, the size of their motions and distances, and their connections on optical and mechanical grounds belong to Astronomy. Mathematical geography, chronology and gnomonics belong with it.
(2) The arts that need mathematics are civil, military, naval and dike architecture. Dike architecture 'still awaits a mathematical form'. Also listed are ship-handling under sail, artillery and pyrotechnics, which the text says are largely non-mathematical.

§2 describes the mathematical method. The Greeks therefore called the doctrine of magnitudes 'the sciences' par excellence (μαθήματα). The method rests on one rule: present first whatever is needed to understand what follows. It therefore proceeds from definitions (Definitiones) and axioms (Axiomata, propositions evident from the definitions) to theorems (Theoremata). The proofs of the theorems show their connection with what was accepted before so clearly that one could not overturn them without overturning the earlier concepts and propositions (the sentence continues on the next page).

The handwritten right margin is cut off at the image edge. It continues onto the next leaf as a bibliography of Euler's academic writings: Commentarii and Novi Commentarii Petropolitani, Acta, Paris Mémoires 1765 (Dioptrique) and 1778 (ship-bow resistance), and the Paris prize pieces (masts, fire, tides, magnetism, Saturn/Jupiter inequalities, ship propulsion without wind, perturbations, rolling and pitching, lunar theory). This is a reading list or catalogue entry, not a derivation.
